title: When the Monsoon Sings
premise: Isandro Coldharbour, a salvage diver hiding from a past she refuses to name, is hired to recover equipment from a wreck the navy officially denies exists. When a government survey team vanishes near the river's forbidden headwaters, she finds their abandoned gear—and evidence that the 'wreck' was a cover for a mining operation poisoning the watershed. Following the river upstream with a disgraced surveyor and a local guide who knows more than he admits, Isandro must choose between exposing the truth that will shatter her hard-won anonymity and staying silent as the water—and everyone downstream—dies. In the end she broadcasts the evidence at the cost of her old life, finding belonging not in invisibility but in the community that rises up beside her.
about_author: Jonah Brightwater is the pen name of a former marine surveyor who spent six years charting rivers no one wanted mapped before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people who measure their lives in distances rather than days.

chapters.title: Ten Miles Deep
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She dives the navy's 'nonexistent' wreck, recovering a sealed crate she was paid not to open, and we learn she counts life in miles logged, not years lived. Emotional beat: controlled isolation, the comfort of rules.

chapters.title: The Crate That Breathes
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Alone in her boathouse, she cracks the crate: water samples, geological charts of the upper river—headwaters marked RESTRICTED. A radio message summons her to salvage a second site. Beat: curiosity cracking the shell of caution.

chapters.title: Gear With No Ghosts
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At the second site she finds the vanished survey team's camp—boots by the fire, instruments still running, no tracks leading out. The river there runs wrong: too warm, faintly iridescent. Beat: dread arriving quietly.

chapters.title: A Surveyor Named Pell
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. Introduce Wren Pell, the survey team's disgraced cartographer who stayed behind at base camp and now begs Isandro to go upstream after her missing colleagues. Beat: guilt meeting opportunity.

chapters.title: The Guide Who Lies Well
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She hires Tamás Oyelaran, a river guide whose family lives downstream of the restricted zone; he agrees too easily, and Isandro notes it. First leg upstream through flooded forest. Beat: wary alliance forming.

chapters.title: Miles Eleven Through Nineteen
chapters.summary: Tamás's POV. Rapids, leeches, and small talk that isn't small: Tamás probes Isandro's past while deflecting questions about why the headwaters matter to him. Beat: two liars recognizing each other.

chapters.title: What the Water Remembers
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. Interlude: Pell decodes the survey team's last transmission—a chemical signature, industrial, dated weeks before any official operation began. Beat: the conspiracy gains a shape.

chapters.title: The Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A navy patrol stops them; Isandro talks her way through using credentials tied to the name she buried ten years ago, burning part of her cover. Beat: the past becomes currency.

chapters.title: Terrace Country
chapters.summary: Tamás's POV. They reach terraced ruins above the gorge—old mining works, newer than they should be, humming with generators. Someone is still operating here. Beat: wonder curdling into alarm.

chapters.title: The Living Camp
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. They find the survey team—not dead, but detained, working under guard for the mining consortium that owns the navy's silence. Among them: someone who recognizes Isandro's real name. Beat: identity exposed, loyalty tested.

chapters.title: Bargaining With Mirrors
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. The consortium offers Isandro everything she lost: reinstatement, records sealed, a future—if she pilots their next shipment downriver and says nothing. Beat: temptation wearing her own face.

chapters.title: Tamás's River
chapters.summary: Tamás's POV. He reveals his stake: his village's wells already run iridescent; children are sick. He didn't guide Isandro for money—he needed a diver to reach the submerged intake valve. Beat: betrayal reframed as desperation.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She dives the flooded mine shaft at the true source and sees the scale of it: a breached tailings pond bleeding into the aquifer, government stamps on every valve. Beat: awe and horror fused.

chapters.title: Nine Miles Down
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Her dive goes wrong—a cave-in, a fouled line—and she survives only because Tamás breaks protocol and follows her down. Beat: trust forged in black water.

chapters.title: The Long Way Back
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. Escaping with the detained surveyors, the group splinters: some take the consortium's amnesty, one sabotages their boats. Beat: loyalty vs. truth made literal in who walks away.

chapters.title: Downstream, Running
chapters.summary: Tamás's POV. Pursued by patrol craft, they run the gorge at flood stage—the monsoon arriving early, the river itself now an adversary. Beat: momentum, sacrifice, Pell injured.

chapters.title: The Village of Gray Wells
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. They reach Tamás's village; Isandro sees the sickness firsthand and meets the people her silence would condemn. Beat: abstraction becomes flesh; resolve hardens.

chapters.title: Everything She Buried
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. To broadcast the evidence they need Isandro's old clearance codes—which means confessing what she did ten years ago to the two people she's come to care for. Beat: the theme's heart; shame met with grace.

chapters.title: The Tower at Mile Zero
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Climax begins: they seize the relay tower at the headwaters during the monsoon peak, Isandro diving the intake to jam the valves while Pell transmits. Beat: every skill, every relationship, converging.

chapters.title: When the Monsoon Sings
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. The broadcast lands; patrols converge; Tamás holds the tower door; the tailings valve seals—or floods the shaft with Isandro inside. Beat: climax at maximum cost.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Aftermath: hearings, headlines, the consortium broken—but Isandro's old name is public, her old life gone. Standing on Tamás's repaired dock, she realizes she stopped counting miles somewhere upstream. Beat: grief and belonging entwined.

chapters.title: Clear Water
chapters.summary: Epilogue, shared POV. One year later: the river runs clear, the village tests its own water, and Isandro—no longer invisible, no longer alone—takes a commission to map the restored headwaters openly. Beat: quiet, earned hope.
